fieldMarks: 4 to 7 1/4 in long, dark brown to grey back with yellowish or white spotting (spotting varies or may be absent).
Solid cream underside; large head relative to body; 15-16 costal grooves.
Expanded toe tips, elongated digits and a moderately prehensile tail for climbing.
behavior: Excellent climber, found up to about 60 ft above ground; nocturnal, hiding by day in leaf litter and retreats.
Surfaces with the first heavy fall rains and stays out until early to mid spring; retreats to tree cavities, rodent burrows and caves in summer.
May share a retreat with up to about eleven others; bites and squeaks when handled. Eats crickets, termites and other invertebrates.
habitat: Coastal live-oak woodland, and yellow pine and black oak forest in the Sierra Nevada foothills; on ground under leaf litter, rocks and logs, and in trees.
A direct developer, not dependent on water for breeding.
range: California Coast Ranges from Humboldt County into Baja California, the central Sierra Nevada foothills, and offshore islands (South Farallon, Santa Catalina, Los Coronados); sea level to about 5,000 ft.
